title: is_stable / stable_plus / quality==1.0 are identical corpus-wide -- documented 4-tier unit-quality scheme collapses to a binary split
purpose: Standalone documentation of a finding first surfaced in omission/artifacts/.lab/real-data-nuisance-and-trialcount-inventory-20260828.json's unit_census_by_session note, per Hamm's explicit instruction to keep this ORTHOGONAL finding separate from the pupil/gaze behavioral-covariate work (this receipt) rather than mixed into it. This receipt does NOT fix or alter any unit-eligibility logic -- it documents the finding plainly so it does not silently affect anything later, per the instruction.

finding.claim: In OmissionSession.get_units(), the columns is_stable, stable_plus, and (quality == 1.0) are IDENTICAL boolean columns -- 0 rows differ -- confirmed directly on at least one real session (sub-C31o_ses-230816_rec: 226 True / 131 False in all three columns simultaneously).
finding.implication: The omission-data skill documents a 4-tier unit-quality scheme (stable_plus / stable / mua / unstable), with stable_plus formally defined as is_stable AND FR>1Hz AND SNR>0.8 AND 100% trial presence, and stable AS is_stable but not stable_plus. If is_stable and stable_plus are identical corpus-wide, then in THIS corpus every unit satisfying is_stable ALSO satisfies the full stable_plus conjunction (FR/SNR/trial-presence), and no unit occupies the 'stable but not stable_plus' tier at all -- collapsing the documented 4-tier scheme to an effective 2-tier (stable_plus-equivalent vs. not-stable) split for any analysis that reads these specific columns.
finding.scope_of_verification: Directly confirmed on 1 session (sub-C31o_ses-230816_rec) by the prior inventory's own audit (2026-08-28); NOT independently re-verified across all 22 sessions by this receipt. This receipt restates and elevates that finding to a standalone, clearly-flagged item per Hamm's instruction -- it does not add new verification breadth.
finding.corpus_wide_totals_from_prior_inventory: 9,061 total units corpus-wide; 4,804 n_stable_plus; 4,257 not-stable (per the prior inventory's Task 2 unit census, which computed these totals across all 22 sessions using the same is_stable/stable_plus/quality columns -- consistent with, but not the same claim as, the single-session column-identity check).

receipts.verification_script: trial_count_audit.py (referenced by the source receipt; uses omission.OmissionSession.get_units() via cached NWB tables in E:/analysis/metadata) -- not re-run by this receipt; restated from the source receipt's own recorded output, per this project's truth-precedence rule that a receipt outranks narrative memory but this receipt is itself transcribing, not re-deriving

doctrine_note: Per this project's tripwire 8 ('check whether a column is constant before interpreting it') and tripwire 9 ('diff a same-named column on the overlap before joining'), any future analysis that treats is_stable, stable_plus, and quality==1.0 as three independently informative unit-selection criteria in this corpus should first re-verify this finding against the SPECIFIC sessions/tables it intends to use, rather than assuming either (a) the documented 4-tier scheme's stable-but-not-stable_plus tier is populated, or (b) this finding automatically holds outside the 1 session and 22-session-total-count evidence cited above.
explicitly_not_done_here: This receipt does not change classify_unit_quality, get_units, unit_census_report, or any unit-eligibility logic in jnwb/ or omission/. No such change is authorized by this task; ANALYSIS-ONLY doctrine (omission/CLAUDE.md) requires documenting, not fixing, an orthogonal finding discovered in passing.
